newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: A variety of negative and positive news led to choppy trade on the South African bond market on Wednesday with traders complaining of a lack of direction in the lead up to the country's 1997/1998 budget.
"It was very messy, very choppy with the market finding no firm direction and quite a few players got their fingers burnt," a trader at a leading bank said.
At 1415 GMT the benchmark R150 bond was at 15.00 percent from an intraday best and worst level of 14.93 percent and 15.08 percent respectively. The stock was at 14.91 percent late on Tuesday.
The day started with a bang as the market digested the unexpected release late on Tuesday of February reserves data which disappointed players.
Total reserves rose to 12.5 bln rand from 11.8 bln in January, but the unexpected use of 2.1 billion rand of foreign credit lines spelt a net 1.4 decline in the figure.
Analysts polled by Reuters had expected an increase to 12.4 billion rand increase without drawing on loan facilities.
"The guys were really caught today...longs were too low and shorts too high so there was a something akin to a whiplash in the market," a second trader commented.

Negative news of the day included the disappointing reserves number, Tuesday's money market shortage which hit its highest levels in at least 14 months and weaker U.S. Treasuries ahead of Federal Reserve governor Alan Greenspan's Homphrey-Hawkins testimony and U.S. jobs data due out on Friday.
But the market took some comfort in the South African Chamber of Business' February business confidence index -- at its highest level since October 1996.
The big boost of the day came from a giant 2.5 billion rand 20-year Eurorand issue from the World bank which prompted the R150 yield to hurtle lower to 14.93 percent -- the day's best.

The 20-year maturity on the issue is a record and even though it will only raise around 185 million rand for the World Bank as it is a zero-coupon bond, is it seen as a vote of confidence in South Africa.
Local traders were reluctant to predict Thursday's direction but said volatility was almost certain to continue as participants squared up positions going into the budget.
Foreigners bought a net 133.00 million rands worth of South African bonds on Tuesday after selling 323.67 million on Monday, the Bond Exchange said.
Nominal cumulative volumes amounted to 5.95 billion rand on Tuesday from 6.42 billion rand on Monday.
The Reserve Bank said the money market shortage leapt to 11.395 billion rand on Tuesday -- mainly due to forex flows in the system -- from 10.548 billion on Monday.
The shortage touched 11.126 billion rand at the end of December 1996, its previous highest level, the bank said.
Three-month NCD rates were quoted slightly higher between 16.55 and 16.70 percent from 16.50 to 16.70 percent while the 90-day BA rate was unmoved at between 15.90 and 16.10 percent.

Compared to the bond market, the rand had a relatively subdued day, trading slightly weaker on the poor reserves number but holding in a tight intraday range around 4.4450 to 4.4600 against the dollar.
"We started weaker on the reserves data, but the top looks capped at the 4.47 level and I expect a 4.43 to 4.47 range ahead of next Wednesday's budget," a senior forex dealer noted.
The tone was nervy ahead of the budget and many players were sidelined waiting for trade to get off the ground again after the event, other dealers said.
At 1415 GMT the currency was at 4.4500/4530 against the dollar from 4.4420/4470 overnight.
Against the crosses, the rand was last quoted at 7.1594/1719 on sterling from 7.1796/1889 and at 0.3844/3850 marks from 0.3852/3855 marks previously.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
